events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven first.** My pier rating is 2 (average), low confidence.
- **St. Joseph is the backup, also about 2.** Its boat results were the strongest, but its pier water is warm and there was no recent upwelling.
- **Skip Muskegon and South Haven, or treat them as last choices (about 1).**
- **If you fish the pier, start with spoons or flies,** the lures that did best on boats. No report describes pier tackle.

## Why
- **Grand Haven has the newest report,** and it describes upwelling-favorable wind in its last three days. Boat fishing there was only average to below average, so I'd expect the pier to be average at best.
- **St. Joseph had the best boat results,** rated excellent on July 10. Those reports are 20 days old, and the pier water there warmed 2 F in the last three days with no upwelling wind, so I'd expect pier action to be weaker than the boat results suggest.
- **Muskegon and South Haven had average boat results** (July 10) and no recent upwelling, so I'd expect them to be weaker on the pier.

## Evidence
**Recent reports (no pier reports in any of the four ports):**
- Grand Haven, July 24 (newest, 6 days old): boat Chinook not rated, coho 1 (below average). Fish were 35 to 100 ft down in 60 to 120 ft of water. Green and orange spoons and white flasher flies worked. Meat rigs and glow plugs caught a few salmon, rated 1 (Grand Haven, 2024-07-24).
- St. Joseph, July 10 (20 days old): boat Chinook and coho rated 4 (excellent). "Most fish were caught on spoons" at 80 to 90 ft (St. Joseph, 2024-07-10).
- South Haven, July 10: boat Chinook and coho rated 2 (average). Rotators and flies worked, at 75 to 80 ft and 105 to 110 ft (South Haven, 2024-07-10).
- Muskegon, July 10: boat salmon rated 2 (average). Meat rigs and flasher flies worked, at 40 to 100 ft down (Muskegon, 2024-07-10).

**Conditions now (the tool returned a backtest summary for the week before July 30, not live data):**
- St. Joseph pier water (satellite): 72 F, up 2 F in the last 3 days, 0 hours of upwelling wind in the last 3 days (St. Joseph, week before 2024-07-30).
- South Haven pier water: 71 F, flat (South Haven, week before 2024-07-30).
- Grand Haven pier water: 68 F, up 4 F in the last 3 days, 2 hours of upwelling wind in the last 3 days (Grand Haven, week before 2024-07-30).
- Muskegon pier water: 73 F, flat in the last 3 days, 5 hours of upwelling wind (Muskegon, week before 2024-07-30).

**Past seasons:** I did not run the similar-weeks lookup, so I have no historical comparison for this temperature.

## Caveats
- **No pier data.** The ratings are my inference from boat reports and pier water conditions, not pier observations.
- **Report age.** The newest report for St. Joseph, South Haven and Muskegon is 20 days old. Only Grand Haven's is recent (July 24).
- **Conditions are not live.** The tool said live data was unavailable and returned a summary for the week before July 30. Check the current buoy and wind before you go.
- **Warm pier water.** Pier water at 71 to 73 F is above the 52 to 58 F range that Chinook prefer (NY DEC guidance). Salmon are likely to stay offshore unless an upwelling brings cold water in, so I'd watch for north or east winds.

## Sources
- Grand Haven, July 24: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3aa7f0e
- July 10 (St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3a7bce5
- July 3 (for context): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3a65224
